note: Proof 3, reflective macro expansion, the fixpoint: the same form expanded until it is no longer a macro call, which is the whole difference between macroexpand-1 and macroexpand. Setup loads lisp/pipeline.el itself on BOTH sides -- the tracked file, not a copy -- through the one form both dialects read: (fboundp 'expand-file-name) is t in Emacs, which needs an absolute name because its `load' searches load-path for a relative one, and nil in kg, whose `load' takes a '/'-containing name as a literal path. The untaken branch is only ever read. So this snapshot is the pinned Emacs' answer for the code kg ships, with nothing to drift.
